rules.title: San Diego Tenant Protection Ordinance (just cause, relocation assistance, buyout rules)
rules.requirement: Landlords may end a covered tenancy only for an at-fault or no-fault just cause stated in the termination notice. For no-fault terminations they must pay or waive 2 months' rent as relocation assistance (3 months if the tenant is 62+ or disabled). Landlords must also give a written notice of protections and follow buyout disclosure rules.
rules.key_value: Relocation assistance: 2 months' rent (3 months for seniors 62+/disabled)
rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7
rules.quoted_span: The purpose of the Ordinance is to require Just Cause for termination of residential tenancies consistent with California Civil Code section 1946.2, to limit the reasons for termination of a residential tenancy, to require greater tenant relocation assistance in specified circumstances and to provide additional tenant protections.
rules.effective_date_note: Fact sheet states 'The Ordinance goes into effect June 24, 2023.' Secondary source (Legal Aid Society of San Diego fact sheet, updated Sept 2023); SDHC portal notice requirement not yet in effect per the sheet.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to tenancies (right to occupy more than 30 days) in residential rental units, including seniors/disabled additional protections.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels; stays of 30 days or less; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8 voucher tenants); mobilehomes subject to MRL; nonprofit hospital/religious/care/transitional housing; school-owned dormitories; owner sharing bathroom/kitchen; owner-occupied single-family renting up to 2 units/bedrooms; owner-occupied duplex; separately alienable units (e.g., condos) owned by non-REIT/corporate/LLC-with-corporate-member landlords with written exemption notice; housing with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes).
rules.interaction: Consistent with Cal. Civ. Code § 1946.2 but provides greater relocation assistance and additional protections.
rules.penalty: Civil action for injunctive/equitable relief and damages including punitive; at least 3x actual economic damages for wrongful eviction; at least 3x required relocation assistance plus actual damages if not paid; attorney's fees; affirmative defense in unlawful detainer.

unverifiable_exemptions: condominiums/separately alienable units owned by individual landlords with written exemption notice
dormitories, nonprofit hospital/religious/care facilities, transitional housing
transient hotels and stays of 30 days or less

rules.conflict_note: Secondary source dated Sept 2023; later amendments not reflected. Ordinance section numbers beyond 98.0705/98.0706 not given.

parsed.doc_summary: Legal Aid Society of San Diego fact sheet (updated Sept 2023) on San Diego's Tenant Protection Ordinance (eff. 2023-06-24): just-cause eviction grounds, exemptions (incl. 15-year CO exemption), notice, relocation assistance (2 or 3 months), buyout agreement rules and remedies.
